scenario: A volcano observatory hires scientists who specialise in igneous petrology OR in satellite-based remote sensing of volcanic unrest. The two specialisms are independent in the applicant population; OR-gate hiring creates a negative correlation among observatory scientists.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (igneous petrology expertise) OR (volcanic remote-sensing expertise)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(petrology | ¬remote_sensing, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(petrology | remote_sensing, selected) and show it equals P(petrology). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between igneous petrology expertise and volcanic remote-sensing expertise.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks volcanic remote-sensing expertise must possess igneous petrology expertise to be admitted — hence P(petrology|¬remote_sensing,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has volcanic remote-sensing expertise is admitted regardless of igneous petrology expertise, so P(petrology|remote_sensing,sel)=P(petrology)=0.42. The gap (1.0 vs 0.42) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between igneous petrology expertise and volcanic remote-sensing expertise observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.42+0.48-0.42×0.48=0.6984. (2) Among candidates without volcanic remote-sensing expertise: only those with igneous petrology expertise are selected → P(petrology|¬remote_sensing,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with volcanic remote-sensing expertise: selected regardless of igneous petrology expertise → P(petrology|remote_sensing,sel)=P(petrology)=0.42. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬remote_sensing raises P(petrology) from 0.42 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.42,0.48
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6984)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.42)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
